chapter: Miles Davis stories and what jazz means
title: Miles Davis clubbed by a policeman outside Birdland
summary: Gil tells how a policeman hit Miles on the head outside Birdland and how a lawyer said the officer was wrong.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well Miles Davis was kind of a pioneer in several things. For example, he was standing out in front of Birdland one night, standing out there smoking a cigarette, getting some air. He was working downstairs and a cop told him to keep moving. (LAUGHTER).

He said, I'm working down here. The cop pulled out his billy club and hit him over the head. He had like I think eight stiches in his head there. to Rushed him off/the hospital right in the middle of the evening.
Yes, can you imagine that. Things like that.
Oh no. But he probably charged him with resisting arrest or something, the way they.......
He finally, I think he wasn't going to sue (but he talked with his lawyer who said the man was purely wrong you know, the policeman was so wrong, unbelievable............
That's the story, that's the story.
